subject: Recap + Procurement Next Steps — BrightPath AI decision owners & initial commercial guardrails
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightpath.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps (discovery)

Jared — thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side and suggested next steps so we keep momentum.

Highlights / pain we heard:
- Production instability: frequent OOMs and evictions during peak inference windows (10–2 PM PT).
- Rising per-token costs from keeping long-lived GPU pools; limited adaptive batching.
- Audit & data residency requirements for some clients (financial vertical) — need VPC/private deployment options.

Current stack you mentioned:
- In-house transformer inference on k8s with GPU node pools (NVIDIA A100s)
- LangChain orchestration, Redis for short-term KV cache, Postgres for metadata
- Single model family (home-grown 30B) with occasional offload to external API for edge cases

Success criteria you shared:
1) Stable <200ms 95p latency for summary endpoints at current QPS
2) 30–40% unit cost reduction through batching/caching/quantization
3) Ability to meet SOC2-like audit requests and VPC isolation for EU/US customers

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Procurement framing doc (attached): initial SOW + commercial guardrails for a pilot (3 months, up to 50k tokens/day).
2) Technical spike: runtime compatibility test — we’ll run a sample trace against a staged model to measure latency and memory behavior.
3) Stakeholder map: can you confirm the procurement approver and technical evaluator? From today we have:
   - Procurement: Vanessa (procurement@brightpath.ai)?
   - Security: Elena Ruiz (cc’d)
   - Eng/Infra evaluator: Jared (you)

Attachments: BrightPath_MVP_SOW_v1.pdf, procurement_checklist.xlsx (light-weight templates).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the spike and loop in our SRE lead (Jonas Weber) on the kernel/quantization discussion.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das

Thanks, Priyom — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement approver is me + Olivia Park (CFO) for commitments over $50k.
- Procurement contact is procurement@brightpath.ai (copied).
- Security will need an inventory of logs and key management options — Elena is leading that.

1) Can you share a short runbook of what access you need for the compatibility test? (SSH/trace export formats)

Happy for Jonas to join the spike. We can fast-track a PO if the pilot metrics look good.

Subject: Internal: pilot commercial guardrails

Looping in Jonas — some practical guardrails for the 3-month pilot:
- Cap: 50k tokens/day or $X/day (TBD with pricing)
- Soft SLA: 99% uptime during pilot windows; rollback window: 30 minutes
- Optional auto-fallback to smaller model family if memory pressure spikes

Jonas — can you prepare a short checklist for the compatibility test (kernel configs, quantization flags, trace export) and an estimate for how long the spike will take (hours on our side + expected access needed)?

If we keep the pilot narrow (1 route, fixed prompt templates), procurement usually signs quicker.

-Marissa

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@brightpath.ai>, Procurement <procurement@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightpath.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Confirming pilot SOW, spike runbook, and decision owners

Jared / Team — moving this to action. Summary and immediate asks so procurement can raise a PO quickly: 

1) Pilot SOW (attached) — 90-day pilot, up to 50k tokens/day. Commercial guardrails: monthly cap line item + 30-day termination with business-day notice. Pricing: see attached ballpark; final rate pending model selection in spike.

2) Spike runbook (below) — please review and confirm access: 
- Deliverables: latency/memory profile, token-cost estimate, fallback model config
- Data needed: 24–48h trace export (prompt + response sizes), one representative prompt set (10 templates), and short-lived role-based access to traces (S3 link or direct upload).
- Access method: secure S3 share (preferred) or VPN’d upload to our intake bucket. No long-term keys required; we’ll use ephemeral credentials.

3) Decision owners / procurement path: 
- PO approval: Jared + Olivia Park (CFO) for >$50k
- Security signoff: Elena Ruiz (security)
- Technical evaluation: Jared + delegated engineer (please confirm name)

Next steps — action items: 
- Jared / Procurement: send a short confirmation that procurement@brightpath.ai can accept a 90-day pilot PO and whether Olivia needs a pre-brief. (target: EOD Aug 31)
- BrightPath: share the 24–48h trace export or grant S3 access (target: Sep 3)
- Redwood (Jonas/Marissa): schedule the spike the week of Sep 7; estimated 2–3 business days to deliver results after we get traces.

If procurement confirms the path, I’ll convert the attached doc to a DocuSign-ready SOW and push a short commercial summary to Olivia to expedite approval.

Thanks — looking forward to moving ahead.

-Priyom

Attachments: BrightPath_MVP_SOW_v1.pdf, procurement_checklist.xlsx
